ENABLE_PRIVATE_LOG_ANALYTICS true Configures Azure Monitor Private Link when network isolation is enabled and a central workspace is not being reused. ALLOW_MIXED_OBSERVABILITY_WORKSPACES false Allows Application Insights and Log Analytics from different sources. DEPLOY_SEARCH_SERVICE true Deploys Azure AI Search. DEPLOY_SPEECH_SERVICE false Deploys Azure AI Speech (SKU S0). DEPLOY_STORAGE_ACCOUNT true Deploys the document storage account.

Bastion tunneling is disabled by default.

docs.title: Hub integration
docs.text:
Use these parameters to connect the spoke virtual network to an existing hub. See Integrate with an existing hub.

Variable Default Description HUB_INTEGRATION_HUB_VNET_RESOURCE_ID None Resource ID of the hub virtual network. HUB_INTEGRATION_CREATE_HUB_PEERING true Creates the peering from the hub side. HUB_INTEGRATION_PEERING_ALLOW_GATEWAY_TRANSIT false Allows gateway transit on the peering. HUB_INTEGRATION_PEERING_USE_REMOTE_GATEWAYS false Uses the hub gateways from the spoke. HUB_INTEGRATION_EGRESS_NEXT_HOP_IP None Private IP of the hub firewall used as the default route. HUB_INTEGRATION_EXISTING_ROUTE_TABLE_RESOURCE_ID None Route table to attach instead of creating one.

docs.title: Existing resources
docs.text:
Set any of these to reuse a resource instead of creating it:

  • EXISTING_VNET_RESOURCE_ID
  • EXISTING_JUMPBOX_RESOURCE_ID
  • EXISTING_BASTION_RESOURCE_ID
  • EXISTING_NAT_GATEWAY_RESOURCE_ID
  • EXISTING_LOG_ANALYTICS_WORKSPACE_RESOURCE_ID
  • EXISTING_APPLICATION_INSIGHTS_RESOURCE_ID

To use private DNS zones that already exist (for example, in a hub subscription), set EXISTING_PRIVATE_DNS_ZONE_<ZONE>_RESOURCE_ID, where <ZONE> is one of:

COGSVCS, OPENAI, AISERVICES, SEARCH, COSMOS, BLOB, KEYVAULT, APPCONFIG, CONTAINERAPPS, ACR, AZUREMONITOR, OMSOPSINSIGHTS, ODSOPSINSIGHTS, AZUREAUTOMATION, APPINSIGHTS.

docs.title: Hosted agent
docs.text:
These parameters apply when the orchestrator runs as a Foundry hosted agent. See Hosted agents.

Variable Default Description DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY hosted-no-panel Application topology. See Topologies. DEPLOY_AAF_AGENT_SVC true Enables the Foundry Agent Service capability host. HOSTED_AGENT_NAME agent-app-orchestrator Name of the hosted agent in the Foundry project. HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE agent-app-orchestrator Repository name of the agent image in Container Registry. HOSTED_CONVERSATION_OWNER_BINDING delegated How conversation ownership is bound to the caller. HOSTED_CONTINUITY_ENABLED false Managed activation state for continuity endpoints. Hosted topology alone does not enable them. See Hosted agents. HOSTED_AGENT_SSE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 60 Idle timeout for streamed responses. PRESERVE_CLASSIC_RUNTIME false Keeps the classic orchestrator Container App while an existing environment moves to hosted. APP_CONFIG_TLS_COMPATIBILITY false Opt-in bootstrap transport for App Configuration and application Key Vault endpoints. Requires the coordinated runtime correction and KEY_VAULT_URI. See Configuration TLS compatibility.

Other hosted defaults: CPU 2, memory 4Gi, Responses protocol 2.0.0, Invocations protocol 1.0.0, capability key ID v1 and capability TTL 900 seconds. The platform configures continuity history with 100 items and 32000 estimated tokens. These are not character limits or a limit on ordinary session chat. See Hosted agents for the continuity activation and history limitations.

For the UI's owner-binding gates, capability signing requirements and conversation-store settings, see UI continuity configuration. These are runtime settings, not additional infrastructure parameters.

PREPARE_HOSTED_AGENT, HOSTED_AGENT_PREPARED and DEPLOY_HOSTED_AGENT are managed by the deployment scripts. Do not set them by hand.

APP_CONFIG_TLS_COMPATIBILITY is a container environment variable, not an App Configuration key: it is read before remote configuration can load. Only true and false are accepted. The foundation's additive KEY_VAULT_URI output provides the deployed vault URI without hardcoding a cloud DNS suffix and is empty when the vault is not deployed. Use the complete manifest-pinned application and infrastructure combination so the loader and hosted definition agree on these inputs.

docs.title: Deployment controls
docs.text:
These variables control hook execution and application selection. Selecting a different application can change which resources are provisioned.

Variable Description BUILD_MODE local uses Docker on the deployment host. acr-task uses Azure Container Registry. Unset values select a mode as described below. RUN_FROM_JUMPBOX false defers post-provision configuration in an isolated deployment. It is not a connectivity bypass. See Post-provision can be deferred. AZURE_SKIP_NETWORK_ISOLATION_WARNING true also defers post-provision configuration in an isolated deployment. PREFLIGHT_SKIP true skips regional and infrastructure preflight checks, not application-definition or topology validation. AGENTLZ_REGIONAL_PREFLIGHT_SKIP true skips only the regional quota and availability check. AGENTLZ_APP_DEFINITION Path to a custom application definition. See Custom applications.

Preflight skip flags are diagnostic controls, not a supported fix for quota, region, permission or network failures. Resolve the reported cause before deploying.

When BUILD_MODE is unset, component scripts first apply recognized legacy USE_DOCKER values. Otherwise, network isolation or a configured task pool selects ACR Tasks. Without either, usable Docker selects a local build, and unavailable Docker selects ACR Tasks. Explicit local fails if Docker is unusable rather than falling back silently.

Hosted orchestrator image preparation always uses ACR Tasks. BUILD_MODE=local does not change that preparation path or the isolated custom source-build path. See Hosted agents and Custom applications.

docs.title: Runtime settings
docs.text:
Post-provision publishes runtime settings to Azure App Configuration with the label agent-lz. Use that label for platform-owned settings.

The bundled components do not read exclusively from agent-lz. Their startup loaders also select service or legacy labels, and later matching selections can overwrite earlier values. UI and ingestion endpoint loaders end with label_filter=None, which leaves the label filter unset and can read other labels. The orchestrator uses the explicit null label "\0" for its last selection, which reads unlabelled keys rather than all labels. Unlabelled values can still override agent-lz values.

Do not rely on labels alone to isolate component configuration or assume that unlabelled values are used only when a key is missing. Check for conflicting legacy, service and unlabelled values before changing a setting. The component repositories document their version-specific selectors.

To change a runtime setting:

  1. Update the key in App Configuration with the label agent-lz.
  2. Restart the affected Container App revision or deploy a new hosted version so it reloads startup configuration. Running hosted versions are immutable.

Deployment-owned keys can be overwritten by the next provision or post-provision run. Change their deployment inputs as well when the new value must persist. Settings declared by a custom application definition are validated but not published. Publish them yourself.

Use the runtime-setting runbook for commands and secret rotation for versioned versus unversioned Key Vault references. Changing deployment selection, RBAC or infrastructure requires the matching full workflow, not just a key edit.

docs.title: Connect Copilot Studio to a private Foundry agent
docs.text:
Connect a Copilot Studio agent to an existing Microsoft Foundry hosted agent without enabling Foundry public network access.

You will reuse the existing Foundry agent and network, then create a relay flow and a dedicated pilot agent in Copilot Studio.

Messages follow this path:

  1. Copilot Studio
  3. Power Automate agent flow
  4. HTTPS request Microsoft Entra ID authentication
  5. Foundry agent Responses API

Private connectivity: the HTTPS request goes through the Power Platform delegated subnet and Foundry private endpoint.

Why use a flow in this scenario?

This runbook covers Foundry with Public Network Access (PNA) disabled. It uses a Power Automate flow because the HTTP connector supports virtual network integration, allowing HTTPS requests to reach Foundry through its private endpoint. The native Microsoft Foundry integration is in preview and follows a separate setup, outside this procedure.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Foundry: A running, tested hosted agent. Ask its owner for the stable Responses URL and active agent version. Use the agent endpoint shown in Step 3, not a Container Apps /invocations URL or an Activity endpoint.
  • Azure network: The platform team has already delivered the Power Platform delegated subnet, regional connectivity, an enterprise policy and its Azure resource ID, an approved Foundry private endpoint and private DNS. Every subnet referenced by the policy must resolve and reach Foundry over HTTPS. Foundry public network access must be Disabled.
  • Power Platform: A Managed Environment with Dataverse, a maker account allowed to create agents, flows and connections, and a Power Platform administrator to associate the enterprise policy. The administrator needs read access to that Azure policy.
  • Governance: Your data policies permit the trigger and HTTP connector together. Confirm Copilot Studio capacity and premium-connector entitlements; this connector is Premium. Azure hosting and model charges are separate. See agent-flow licensing.

Creating Azure network resources is outside this procedure. A subnet alone is not sufficient: the enterprise policy must reference the required regional networks and be associated with the environment. Use the Power Platform setup requirements if the platform handoff is incomplete.

Foundry uses the connection user's permissions

This procedure uses a specific, shared connection signed in as an approved Microsoft Entra user in the Foundry tenant. Foundry sees that connection user, not automatically the person chatting in Studio. Do not use it for user-specific document permissions unless your application independently enforces them. Require authentication, restrict the Studio agent to approved users and approve the data they can all access.

Per-user connections require a separate identity and channel design; they are not enabled by forwarding a user name in the prompt. See flow connection credentials.

docs.title: Step 1: Associate the environment with the private network
docs.text:
A Power Platform administrator performs this step. Schedule the change first: the environment's other supported workloads are also affected, and connections can be unstable for up to 30 minutes.

  1. In the Power Platform admin center, open Manage > Environments, select the target environment and record its Environment ID from Details. Select this same environment in Copilot Studio and Power Automate.
  2. Open Security > Data and privacy > Azure Virtual Network policies. Select the environment, select the prepared policy and Save. If the correct association already exists, leave it unchanged.
  3. Open Manage > Environments, select the environment, then History. Wait for the policy operation to show Succeeded before testing.
  4. Have the platform team confirm private DNS, routing and HTTPS access from each delegated regional subnet, not just from the jumpbox.
  5. In the Azure portal, open the Foundry resource's Networking settings. Confirm public network access is Disabled and the intended private endpoint connection is Approved. Do not change either setting to get a successful test.

Expected result: The Managed Environment is linked to the intended policy, and all its regional paths can reach the Foundry private endpoint.

docs.title: Step 2: Authorize the connection user
docs.text:
Have an authorized Azure RBAC administrator grant the connection user Foundry Agent Consumer on the specific agent, if equivalent access is not already present. This allows invocation without authoring access. The agent's own identity and downstream permissions are separate; do not replace them with the connection user's identity.

PowerShell: grant access to this agent only

Run with PowerShell 7 and Azure CLI. Replace every placeholder; use the object ID of the user who will sign in to the connection, not an app client ID. Copy Object ID from that user's Overview in the Microsoft Entra admin center.

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

$subscriptionId = "<subscription-id>"
$agentScope = "/subscriptions/$subscriptionId/resourceGroups/<resource-group>/providers/Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/<foundry-resource>/projects/<project>/agents/<agent>"
$connectionUserObjectId = "<connection-user-object-id>"

az login
az account set --subscription $subscriptionId
az role assignment create `
    --assignee-object-id $connectionUserObjectId `
    --assignee-principal-type User `
    --role "eed3b665-ab3a-47b6-8f48-c9382fb1dad6" `
    --scope $agentScope `
    --query "{id:id,scope:scope}" --output json

Expected result: The assignment targets the intended user and agent. Keep the returned id for rollback if this is a new pilot-only grant, and allow time for the permissions to take effect. Do not grant subscription Owner, broad Contributor or extra project-authoring roles to resolve an invocation failure. See Foundry RBAC and agent scopes.

docs.title: Step 3: Create the authenticated agent flow
docs.text:
In Copilot Studio, select Flows > New flow > Agent flow. Use the environment from Step 1 and name the flow Call private Foundry agent. Keep it in a solution so it can be moved with its connection reference; the solution is the deployment package for these items.

Use the flow's expression editor

In this step, paste expressions into the flow designer's Expression editor (fx), not as plain text. Step 4 uses Copilot Studio's Formula tab instead.

docs.title: Input and connection
docs.text:
1. In When an agent calls the flow, add one Text input named message. Open the trigger's Code view / Peek code and find the property whose title is message. Its generated key is text in the tested designer; message is only the display name. Use the actual key in the body expression.
  2. Between the trigger and Respond to the agent, add Invoke an HTTP request from HTTP with Microsoft Entra ID (preauthorized). Do not use Get web resource; it is not supported with VNet delegation.
  3. Create a connection with Log in with Microsoft Entra ID, using:
Connection field Value Microsoft Entra ID Resource URI (Application ID URI) https://ai.azure.com Base Resource URL https://<foundry-resource>.services.ai.azure.com Sign-in account The connection user authorized in Step 2

"Preauthorized" refers to the Microsoft application used by the connector, not to access to your Foundry agent. Requests still use HTTPS and the connection user's Microsoft Entra identity, with the permissions from Step 2.

Do not append the project path to the base URL or use the resource hostname as the token audience. Do not supply a bearer token, API key or client secret. If tenant policy blocks the connector or requires consent, stop and have the administrator review the connector's permission requirements; do not bypass the policy with another connector.

docs.title: HTTPS request
docs.text:
Keep the action name Invoke an HTTP request. The expressions below reference its internal name, Invoke_an_HTTP_request; check that name in Code view if the designer adds a suffix. If it differs, update every body(...) reference in the response expression below.

Request field Value Method POST URL The fixed agent Responses URL below Header Content-Type: application/json Retry policy None for the pilot; a repeated POST can duplicate work 
https://<foundry-resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>/agents/<agent>/endpoint/protocols/openai/responses?api-version=v1

Use the exact stable Responses URL from the agent's Publish dropdown in Foundry, or ask its owner for it. Do not substitute display names into the template. Do not let the chat user or generative orchestration choose the URL, method, headers or connection.

API version is not the agent version

Keep api-version=v1 unchanged. Foundry selects the active agent version behind the stable URL; do not add that version to the URL. Record and verify it before acceptance.

For Body, select Expression and paste this expression, without @{...}:

string(setProperty(json('{"store":true,"stream":false}'), 'input', triggerBody()?['text']))

Replace text only if the trigger uses another property. Constructing the object before serializing it preserves quotes, line breaks, backslashes and Unicode. Do not concatenate the user's message into a JSON string.

The flow waits for a complete response; it does not stream tokens. store:true requests response storage; approve Foundry's retention settings before using real data. It does not implement multi-turn history: each call sends only the current message.

docs.title: Response and publication
docs.text:
In Respond to the agent, add a Text output named foundry_response. Set its value using Expression:

if(contains(body('Invoke_an_HTTP_request'), '$content'), base64ToString(body('Invoke_an_HTTP_request')?['$content']), string(body('Invoke_an_HTTP_request')))

This decodes the response to JSON text, whether the connector returns JSON directly or inside a base64 $content envelope. It is not the chat reply; Step 4 extracts that text.

Select Respond to the agent > Settings and configure:

  • Run After: Run only when Invoke an HTTP request is successful. Do not select failed, skipped or timed-out states.
  • Networking: Set Asynchronous response = Off.

Save and Publish the flow. In Power Automate, open its details page, then Run only users > Edit. For the HTTP connector, select the specific authorized connection, not Provided by run-only user, and save the settings.

In Solutions, open your team's solution and confirm the flow is listed. If not, select Add existing > Automation > Cloud flow, select the flow and Add. If needed, create a solution first.

Expected result: The published flow has one text input, one authenticated POST and one text output. Its complete synchronous execution must stay within the 100-second agent-action limit. Streaming and background completion are not handled by this relay.

docs.title: Step 4: Relay the actual response in Copilot Studio
docs.text:
In Copilot Studio, create or open a dedicated pilot agent. The topic below handles every nonempty message; do not add it unchanged to an agent with other routing responsibilities. Require user authentication and restrict sharing before adding real users.

  1. Open Topics > Add a topic > From blank and name it Private Foundry relay. On the Trigger node, select Change trigger > A message is received, then Edit. In the trigger's Condition, switch Builder > Formula and enter !IsBlank(System.Activity.Text). This is a trigger property, not a separate Condition node.
  2. Add Add a tool, select the published Call private Foundry agent flow, and bind its message input to the system variable System.Activity.Text (the user's current message). For foundry_response, create a Text topic variable named FoundryResponse, shown as Topic.FoundryResponse.

  3. Add Variable management > Set a variable value. Under Set variable, select Create new and name the variable FoundryReply (shown as Topic.FoundryReply). For To value, select Formula and paste the expression below; the resulting variable must be Text. It reads all message output_text parts, rather than assuming the first output item is a message; tool calls can precede it.

    Power Fx: extract text only from a completed, error-free response 

    IfError(
    With(
        { r: ParseJSON(Topic.FoundryResponse) },
        If(
            Text(r.status) = "completed" && IsBlank(r.error),
            Concat(
                Filter(Table(r.output), Text(Value.type) = "message") As m,
                Concat(
                    Filter(Table(m.Value.content), Text(Value.type) = "output_text") As c,
                    Text(c.Value.text),
                    Char(10)
                ),
                Char(10)
            ),
            Blank()
        )
    ),
    Blank()
)

  4. Add a Condition node. In its ... menu, select Change to formula, open the formula editor and enter IsBlank(Topic.FoundryReply) || IsMatch(Topic.FoundryReply, "\s*", MatchOptions.Complete). In the true branch (missing or whitespace-only text), send: "The Foundry agent did not return a completed text response. Please contact the support team." Do not display raw JSON or retry the POST automatically. In All Other Conditions (false), add Send a message and insert the Topic.FoundryReply variable, without a generative rewrite. Insert its value with the variable picker; do not type its name as message text.

  5. End both branches with Topic management > End all topics. Do not enable a second Foundry tool as an automatic fallback. Run the topic checker and resolve every error before saving.

    6. Expected result: One message invokes the flow once and displays Foundry's actual text. Invalid JSON, an incomplete/failed response or missing text produces an explicit failure message. If the HTTP action itself fails, Studio's error handling must report the failed action, not substitute a generated answer.

docs.title: Step 5: Verify the private path, then publish
docs.text:
Use harmless test data in a new Studio test conversation and record the UTC test window. In Power Automate, open the flow's details page and select the matching run in Run history. Keep its run ID; expand the HTTP action to inspect its status and outputs, and Respond to the agent for the decoded JSON. A chatbot reply alone is not proof of backend execution.

Check Acceptance evidence Request integrity A message containing "quotes", a newline, C:\test\file and café reaches the flow unchanged. Use an echo-capable test agent if exact round-trip comparison is needed. Real Foundry execution The matching flow run shows HTTP 200, decoded status: completed, no non-null error, and real output_text. Check the selected agent/version in available response or runtime diagnostics. Private ingress Foundry public network access is still Disabled. Have the platform team correlate the UTC test window and target resource with existing Foundry gateway diagnostics or equivalent approved network evidence; the source must be the delegated private path, not a public connector address. No hidden fallback The topic trace invokes the intended flow once and sends its returned text. A failed action or invalid response gives an error, not a plausible generated reply. Authorization An approved pilot user can invoke the Studio agent; a user outside the shared audience cannot. Separately confirm that the connection identity and agent cannot expose data outside the approved shared-data boundary. Runtime limit Representative calls complete below 100 seconds, including connector and agent processing.

Use existing approved diagnostic settings; do not turn on prompt or document capture just to obtain network evidence. A jumpbox success establishes only the jumpbox path. If gateway logs are unavailable, do not claim that private ingress has been independently verified.

After these checks pass, return to the Studio agent and select Publish. Repeat the test from the intended authenticated channel with an approved pilot user. Designer success does not verify channel authentication, sharing or connection behavior.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Check and action Public access is disabled / HTTP 403 Confirm the flow ran in the associated environment, uses Invoke an HTTP request from the exact connector, and the policy operation succeeded. Inspect the ingress source before changing RBAC. Do not enable Foundry public network access. DNS failure or timeout Have the platform team check DNS, peering/routes, NSGs and HTTPS from every delegated regional subnet. Each path referenced by the policy must reach the private endpoint. HTTP 401 / authorization 403 Verify the connection user's tenant, https://ai.azure.com audience, connection health and agent-scoped invocation access. Distinguish connector-consent errors from Foundry RBAC errors; allow role propagation. HTTP 404 / unsupported endpoint Compare the fixed URL, project and agent with the tested stable Responses endpoint. Do not substitute Activity, Container Apps or another API version. Response contains $content, or Studio shows base64 Apply the Step 3 decoder and check the HTTP action's internal name. Failed/empty response despite HTTP 200 Inspect the decoded response status, error and output types in restricted run history. The agent must return a completed text response; the relay does not render files or handle tool approvals. Flow is missing from the tool picker Check the selected environment, solution membership, published state and required trigger/response actions. Topic checker rejects the formula Confirm Topic.FoundryResponse is Text, paste into the Formula tab, and preserve the As m / As c aliases. Use commas as Power Fx argument separators. Studio action times out Check full execution time and synchronous response settings. Optimize the agent or design an explicit asynchronous integration; do not increase retries or send a fake success.

Restrict run-history access. Once validation is complete, apply your organization's Secure inputs / Secure outputs policy to the HTTP and response actions: these can contain prompts, retrieved data and replies. Share only sanitized UTC timestamps, run/request IDs and status codes during diagnosis.

docs.title: Operate or stop the integration
docs.text:
• Change: Export/version the solution and record the endpoint, active agent version and connection reference before editing. Rebind the connection in each target environment and repeat Step 5 after an agent, policy or identity change.
  • Maintain: Assign an owner for connection reauthentication, monitor failures, latency and capacity, and review access and response-retention policies. This relay supplies neither multi-turn history nor the chat user's identity in Foundry.
  • Stop: Disable the relay topic/flow and republish the Studio agent. Remove a pilot-only role assignment only if it was created for this integration and is not shared. Do not delete the delegated subnet or detach the environment's VNet policy as routine rollback: other workloads may depend on it. Keep Foundry public network access disabled throughout.

docs.title: Full stack deploy
docs.text:
Deploy the Azure foundation and the bundled agent application: a web UI, an orchestrator and, when selected, an ingestion application. Choose where the orchestrator runs and how the deployment connects to Azure before provisioning.

Only need the foundation? Use Deploy infrastructure only. For the relationship between the template, its manifest and lifecycle hooks, see How the template works.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Permissions: Owner, or Contributor plus User Access Administrator, at the required deployment scopes. Shared networks, DNS and monitoring can require additional permissions in their own scopes. See Permissions.
  • Subscription readiness: accepted Responsible AI terms, registered resource providers, supported service/model regions and sufficient quota for the selected parameters. Regional considerations explain why passing preflight does not guarantee available capacity.
  • Private deployments: an authorized VPN/VNet-connected deployment host with private DNS resolution. An ACR Tasks build pool is not that host.
Tool Required for Azure Developer CLI (azd) and Azure CLI (az) Provisioning and lifecycle hooks; use current supported versions PowerShell 7 Windows hooks and cross-platform preflight checks Bash, jq and curl on Linux/macOS POSIX hooks and dependency bootstrap Git Fetching selected, pinned application sources Python 3.12 with pip and venv Validation, composition and service configuration Docker, when using local builds Optional for supported Container App builds; hosted preparation uses ACR Tasks Foundry agents azd extension (azure.ai.agents) Hosted deployment; install with azd extension install azure.ai.agents if absent

Cost and time

Provisioning creates billable resources before the application is ready. Review the foundation inventory and cost scenarios and cost guide, then budget for application runtime, model usage and data. First deployments take longer because of resource creation, image builds, role propagation and private-link approvals. There is no fixed completion time.

docs.title: Step 1: Get the code
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Azure/agent-landing-zone.git
cd agent-landing-zone

The repository's default main branch is the stable deployment source, not develop. Record the resolved commit for repeatable deployments. To deliberately select a published release instead, use git fetch --tags and git checkout <release-tag> before continuing.

Alternatively, azd init -t Azure/agent-landing-zone initializes the current default template in an empty directory. Reuse the environment it creates rather than creating it again in Step 2.

docs.title: Prepare Python
docs.text:
From the repository root:

python -m venv .venv

On Linux/macOS, use python3 if python is unavailable. Activate .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 in PowerShell or source .venv/bin/activate in Bash, then install:

python -m pip install -r config/requirements.txt

Keep this environment active for the lifecycle commands.

docs.title: Working from your own repository
docs.text:
An unmodified deployment needs only the platform checkout. Hooks fetch selected runtime components automatically; four forks are not required. Fork or mirror the platform when you maintain deployment inputs or automation, and fork only the runtime components whose source you change.

Keep reviewed, nonsecret inputs in source control and apply them explicitly with azd env set; an environments/ folder is not loaded automatically. Protect .azure/, credentials, sibling component workspaces and deployment logs. For private components, configure Git read access on the actual deployment host separately from Azure authentication. Never embed tokens in repository URLs. See Custom applications for source pinning and composition.

docs.title: Step 2: Select the deployment target
docs.text:
The following creates a new environment. Replace all placeholders:

az login
azd auth login
az account set --subscription <subscription-id>
azd env new <environment-name>
azd env set AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID <subscription-id>
azd env set AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP <dedicated-resource-group>
azd env set AZURE_LOCATION <region>

For an existing environment, use azd env select <environment-name> instead and preserve its approved inputs. Use separate environments, resource groups, identities, secrets and data for DEV, TEST and PROD. An environment name or the App Configuration label alone is not a security boundary. Promote the same reviewed source revision with stage-specific inputs.

docs.title: Step 3: Choose the application and network
Orchestrator topology
docs.text:
DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY chooses where the agent orchestrator runs. It is independent of the foundation's standalone or hub-and-spoke network shape.

Value Orchestrator runs in Administrative panel Application Cosmos DB hosted-no-panel Foundry Agent Service Not deployed Not deployed hosted-panel Foundry Agent Service Deployed Deployed classic Azure Container Apps Not applicable Deployed

A new environment defaults to hosted-no-panel. To choose another value before first provision, for example Container Apps:

azd env set DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY classic

Existing environments retain their recorded topology. Older environments without a topology marker resolve to classic; do not change them merely to match a new-install default. The table describes application resources, not the Foundry Agent Service's separate backing resources. See Hosted agents for identity, continuity and panel semantics.

docs.title: Ingestion and custom applications
docs.text:
Fresh environments default to DEPLOY_INGESTION_CONTAINER_APP=false, using native Foundry IQ ingestion for the configured default Blob source. Select the optional app before provisioning if its ingestion features or eligible conversation uploads are required:

azd env set DEPLOY_INGESTION_CONTAINER_APP true

This does not switch the retrieval backend or rewrite source/index bindings. Existing environments keep their selection. Before disabling an existing app, review ingestion choices and the older-UI migration warning. Disabling uploads must not be inferred from a missing endpoint.

For a different application, set AGENTLZ_APP_DEFINITION to its definition path before the first provision. The environment binds to that application ID. Use Custom applications for its contract and component-specific deployment requirements; do not substitute bundled hosted preparation for a custom definition's build flow.

docs.title: Network and build mode
docs.text:
Choose one network posture for this new environment:

Choice Inputs and preparation Public service endpoints azd env set NETWORK_ISOLATION false; authentication and authorization still apply Private, self-contained network azd env set NETWORK_ISOLATION true; review the standalone design Private spoke using an existing hub NETWORK_ISOLATION=true, explicit hub routing, peering, DNS and shared-service inputs from the hub-and-spoke reference Existing VNet Review subnet ownership, delegations, NSGs and BYO parameters before enabling USE_EXISTING_VNET

Apply the approved foundation inputs from infrastructure choices. Do not change NETWORK_ISOLATION on an existing environment as a retry shortcut. With isolation enabled, run configuration, preparation and deployment from the connected host. If creating that host first, use the deferred post-provision procedure.

Image build path Selection Public registry, remote builds azd env set BUILD_MODE acr-task; supported components use regular ACR Tasks Private registry, remote builds Keep DEPLOY_ACR_TASK_AGENT_POOL=true before provision and use BUILD_MODE=acr-task; builds use the provisioned VNet pool Supported Container Apps, local Docker azd env set BUILD_MODE local; the host must reach the registry and service endpoints

Automatic hosted image preparation and isolated custom source builds still require the private pool. BUILD_MODE=local is not a local-build alternative for those paths. See network isolation for build egress, DNS and private-link readiness requirements.

docs.title: Step 4: Deploy
docs.text:
Confirm the target before creating or changing resources:

azd env get-value AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID
azd env get-value AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP
azd hooks run preup

Resolve validation, quota, Policy and connectivity failures rather than bypassing checks. The explicit preup check also validates binding before standalone provisioning, which otherwise runs its check after azd may initialize a resource group.

docs.title: Container Apps orchestrator (classic)
docs.text:
azd up

This runs provisioning, post-provision service configuration, image builds and application deployment.

docs.title: Foundry orchestrator (hosted-no-panel or hosted-panel)
docs.text:
Confirm the runner has Foundry agent authoring access on the exact project (Foundry User, previously Azure AI User, or an appropriate equivalent), account read access and the required scoped role-assignment authority. Azure sign-in or network connectivity alone is insufficient; see private-runner permissions and hosted identities.

A fresh bundled hosted deployment needs this order:

azd provision
pwsh scripts/prepareHostedDeployment.ps1
azd provision
azd deploy

On Linux/macOS replace the preparation command with ./scripts/prepareHostedDeployment.sh.

Stage Result First provision Creates the foundation and configures its services Preparation Fetches the pinned orchestrator source, builds its hosted image and records an immutable digest Second provision Materializes the image and Foundry deployment handoff Deploy Creates the hosted version, bootstraps runtime access, smoke-tests it and deploys the other selected apps

A fresh azd up does not build the missing hosted handoff. If you started with it, complete preparation, the second provision and deployment. If the first provision deferred configuration, complete that work before preparation. Do not skip the second provision or replace the digest with an image tag. If the second provision rejects quota for an unchanged deployment, inspect quota diagnostics rather than bypassing the gate.

For an already configured infrastructure-only environment, reuse the same checkout, inputs and bound application. In classic, continue with azd deploy. In a bundled hosted topology, continue at preparation above.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
1. Inspect the selected resource group and intended deployed revisions, not just an older healthy placeholder:

    azd env get-value AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP
az containerapp list -g <resource-group> \
  --query "[].{name:name,state:properties.runningStatus,revision:properties.latestReadyRevisionName}" -o table

  2. Open the frontend URL from the deployment outputs or its Container App ingress configuration. Private endpoints require a connected browser. Complete Entra sign-in and delegated-authentication configuration for the intended users.

  3. Exercise an agent task and its configured tools with representative identities. If using documents, add a test document to the configured source, confirm its ingestion, and test both allowed and denied document access. Test uploads only when the ingestion app and upload eligibility are selected.
  4. In a hosted topology, verify the intended routed version and runtime telemetry as well as the remaining Container Apps. A greeting smoke test is not evidence of user login, OBO or document authorization.

Use Troubleshooting for failures. Do not authorize a cutover based only on a successful hook or HTTP 200.

To make a hosted agent available in Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot, continue with Publish to Teams and M365. Bot creation and channel publication are separate manual tasks, not part of this deployment.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text: Run these tasks from the platform root with the intended environment selected, Python active, both CLIs authenticated and private connectivity available when required. Record the source revision, manifest, definition, approved inputs and hosted digest before a change. Back up configuration and relevant data using service-specific procedures.

docs.title: Upgrade to a new release
docs.text:
1. Read the target release notes, component versions and migrations. Upgrade the compatible platform combination, including its repository-owned infra/, rather than independent component tips.
  2. Fetch and check out the approved release tag. Reconcile local platform/runtime changes and update bundled manifest/definition pins together.
  3. Preserve the existing topology, ingestion selection, resource naming and source/index bindings. Follow ingestion migration guidance before opting out or downgrading an older UI.
  4. Run the matching deployment workflow. For a generated hosted image with a changed source pin, prepare it again and provision its handoff before deployment. Validate in DEV before promoting the same revision.
  5. Repeat the application checks, including authorization and any ingestion, history or continuity features in use.

GPT-RAG v3 environments

A v3 environment cannot be upgraded in place to Agent Landing Zone v4. Deploy a new environment, migrate the required documents, indexes and conversation data, and validate it before retiring the old environment.

docs.title: Redeploy applications only
docs.text:
When foundation outputs, application binding, component selection and the image handoff remain compatible:

azd deploy

Bundled Container Apps use the manifest's verified sibling checkouts. Preserve local work and relocate a stale checkout so the hook can fetch the selected revision; it does not advance an existing checkout automatically. Child logs are under each component's .logs directory and can contain sensitive details.

Hosted deployment reuses the prepared digest. A changed generated source pin or image requires preparation, provisioning the handoff and deployment again. An operator-managed digest is not rebuilt automatically: verify its provenance, compatibility and registry availability. Rebuilding identical source separately in each environment does not prove identical image digests.

Infrastructure, RBAC, topology or ingestion-selection changes require the full workflow, not deploy-only. Changing a selection does not delete previously deployed resources or revoke old permissions; retirement is separately authorized.

docs.title: Change a runtime setting
docs.text:
First check configuration ownership and overwrite behavior. Provisioning-managed inputs must be changed in their source and applied through the full workflow. For a directly managed, nonsecret runtime key:

az appconfig kv set --endpoint <app-config-endpoint> --auth-mode login \
  --key <KEY> --value <value> --label agent-lz --yes

Restart each affected Container App revision to reload it:

az containerapp revision restart -g <resource-group> -n <container-app-name> \
  --revision <revision-name>

For a hosted version, run root azd deploy with the compatible handoff. Process environment inputs declared in hosted-agent/azure.yaml are immutable version inputs and require a new agent version. An App Configuration edit cannot replace a process-only setting such as APP_CONFIG_TLS_COMPATIBILITY. The agent-lz label is not an environment-isolation mechanism.

docs.title: Rotate a secret
docs.text: Inspect the Key Vault reference before rotating. An unversioned URI resolves the current secret version when configuration reloads; a versioned URI must be updated deliberately. Add the new secret version through your approved secure process, preserve required access, then restart affected Container App revisions or redeploy the hosted version. Verify the new credential before retiring the old one. Never place secrets in plaintext App Configuration or command logs.

docs.title: Recover hosted runtime access
docs.text:
The bundled post-deploy hook normally bootstraps the discovered runtime principal. To review the exact read-only role plan from the root's selected environment:

python -m config.deployment.hosted_access --azd-env --plan

An authorized administrator can reconcile only that plan with the idempotent wrapper:

pwsh scripts/bootstrapHostedAccess.ps1

On Linux/macOS use ./scripts/bootstrapHostedAccess.sh. The wrapper selects hosted-agent / orchestrator-agent by default; custom services use their own project/service context. Allow role propagation, then retry root azd deploy so the greeting and remaining deployment gates run before cutover.

The closed bootstrap set grants App Configuration Data Reader, model access and, when configured, access to the exact audit secret. It is not a grant to delegated users or a replacement for all capability profiles. Do not grant Owner or remove unrelated assignments to recover. See hosted identities.

docs.title: Roll back to a previous release
docs.text:
Review migration constraints and restore the previous complete compatible combination and its inputs. When only classic application pins changed and the foundation remains compatible:

git checkout <previous-release-tag>
azd deploy

If infrastructure or configuration changed, review and rerun the full workflow. Hosted rollback requires the previous pinned image to be prepared, or its verified digest deliberately restored, then provisioned and deployed. Checking out an old tag does not reverse data migrations. Restore ingestion requirements before downgrading to a UI without the upload gate. Some changes require forward repair or a new environment with data migration. azd down --purge is not rollback.

docs.title: Remove an environment
docs.text:
Destructive action

Confirm the subscription, resource group and deletion prompt. Export or back up required documents, indexes, configuration and conversation data. Check retention obligations and shared-resource dependencies first.

azd env select <environment-name>
azd env get-value AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID
azd env get-value AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP
azd down

Use --purge only when permanent removal of supported soft-deleted resources is explicitly intended. It removes recovery options. Reused resources outside the deletion scope and manually created links can remain and continue incurring charges. For a spoke, retire only its own hub peering/DNS links with their owners; do not delete shared hub, DNS or monitoring resources.

docs.title: Related runbooks
docs.text:
• Connect Copilot Studio to a private Foundry agent
  • Deploy infrastructure only
  • Deploy with Azure DevOps — optional reviewed promotion and automation

docs.title: Deploy infrastructure only
docs.text:
Provision the Azure foundation without building or deploying application images. This is the infrastructure procedure for both Agent Landing Zone and the standalone AI Landing Zone Bicep foundation. Choose the source first: their hooks, parameter files and outputs are not interchangeable.

To run the agent application as well, use Deploy the full stack.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Complete the permissions and tooling prerequisites. The upstream foundation requires Git, Azure CLI, azd and PowerShell 7; the Agent platform additionally requires Python and the platform hook dependencies. Review the resource inventory and cost scenarios and regional capacity caveats. Infrastructure-only still creates billable resources.

The effective footprint is the combination of enabled services, resource-reuse inputs, application definition, orchestrator topology and network settings. This affects AI services and their backing resources, runtimes, data stores, monitoring, networking and optional add-ons—not just one or two services. Use the selected source's main.parameters.json, Bicep conditions and preview as the authority; the foundation inventory is not an Agent application bill of materials.

docs.title: Agent Landing Zone foundation
docs.text:
Use this source if you will deploy the bundled agent application or a compatible custom application later:

git clone https://github.com/Azure/agent-landing-zone.git
cd agent-landing-zone

Follow Python setup. Run all lifecycle commands from this root, not from infra/. Its infra/ is repository-owned source, and manifest.json records the coordinated component pins and upstream foundation provenance.

docs.title: AI Landing Zone foundation without the Agent platform
docs.text:
Use this source for independent foundation resources and their placeholder app:

git clone https://github.com/Azure/bicep-ptn-aiml-landing-zone.git
cd bicep-ptn-aiml-landing-zone

Run from that repository's root, where its main.bicep, main.parameters.json and azure.yaml live. Its lifecycle does not configure or deploy the Agent application. Do not provision this separate project into an Agent environment. For application deployment, start from the Agent source instead.

Both clones use the current default main, not develop. Record the resolved commit and reviewed nonsecret inputs for repeatability. The full-stack source guidance explains optional release selection.

docs.title: Step 2: Create and confirm the target
docs.text:
Replace the placeholders for a new, dedicated environment:

az login
azd auth login
az account set --subscription <subscription-id>
azd env new <environment-name>
azd env set AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID <subscription-id>
azd env set AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP <dedicated-resource-group>
azd env set AZURE_LOCATION <region>

Use azd env select <environment-name> for an existing environment and keep its approved inputs. Use separate environment, resource-group, identity, configuration and data boundaries for each stage; protect local .azure/ state. Fork or mirror the source only when maintaining your own inputs or automation.

docs.title: Step 3: Choose the foundation shape
docs.text: The following choices apply before provisioning. DEPLOYMENT_MODE records the network design intent; it does not configure routing, DNS or isolation by itself. It is separate from Agent's DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY, which chooses the orchestrator.

docs.title: Public service endpoints
docs.text:
azd env set NETWORK_ISOLATION false
azd env set DEPLOYMENT_MODE standalone

Service authentication and authorization still apply. This is not a private deployment or a way to repair an existing private environment.

docs.title: Private standalone network
docs.text:
azd env set NETWORK_ISOLATION true
azd env set DEPLOYMENT_MODE standalone
azd env set DEPLOY_AZURE_FIREWALL true
azd env set DEPLOY_JUMPBOX true
azd env set DEPLOY_BASTION true
azd env set DEPLOY_NAT_GATEWAY true

Review the standalone reference for nonoverlapping subnets, NSGs, egress and private DNS. For native Bastion RDP, choose BASTION_SKU_NAME=Standard and BASTION_ENABLE_TUNNELING=true; portal access does not require the native tunneling workflow. Have a connected host ready for Agent post-provision configuration, or use explicit deferral below.

docs.title: Private spoke using an existing hub
docs.text:
Agree hub routing, reverse peering, DNS and permissions with their owners first. For a new spoke VNet with a hub firewall:

azd env set NETWORK_ISOLATION true
azd env set DEPLOYMENT_MODE ailz-integrated
azd env set DEPLOY_AZURE_FIREWALL false
azd env set DEPLOY_BASTION false
azd env set DEPLOY_NAT_GATEWAY false
azd env set DEPLOY_JUMPBOX true
azd env set EXISTING_BASTION_RESOURCE_ID <hub-bastion-resource-id>
azd env set HUB_INTEGRATION_HUB_VNET_RESOURCE_ID <hub-vnet-resource-id>
azd env set HUB_INTEGRATION_CREATE_HUB_PEERING true
azd env set HUB_INTEGRATION_EGRESS_NEXT_HOP_IP <hub-firewall-private-ip>

Instead of a next-hop IP, a platform-managed route table can be selected with HUB_INTEGRATION_EXISTING_ROUTE_TABLE_RESOURCE_ID; these inputs are mutually exclusive. Do not leave both unset if hub egress is required. Shared monitoring uses EXISTING_LOG_ANALYTICS_WORKSPACE_RESOURCE_ID and, when applicable, EXISTING_APPLICATION_INSIGHTS_RESOURCE_ID with its protected connection string.

Apply the hub-and-spoke DNS and peering contract before provisioning. A network operator may need to complete reverse peering and DNS links as soon as a fresh spoke VNet exists, before bootstrap can finish. The upstream test-hub fixture is not a production connectivity deployment.

docs.title: Existing networks, private DNS and parameter files
docs.text:
Choice Required review Existing VNet Set USE_EXISTING_VNET=true and EXISTING_VNET_RESOURCE_ID. Decide who owns subnets, NSGs and delegations before setting DEPLOY_SUBNETS; both peering directions are externally managed for BYO VNet Shared private DNS Supply the applicable EXISTING_PRIVATE_DNS_ZONE_*_RESOURCE_ID inputs. Their owner supplies VNet links or resolver forwarding; peering alone does not propagate DNS Azure Policy-managed DNS Use POLICY_MANAGED_PRIVATE_DNS=true instead of BYO zone overrides and agree who creates zone groups, records and links Approved public exception Review native allowedIpRanges and Storage trusted-service/resource-instance exceptions explicitly; isolation is not a blanket public-access guarantee Controlled public frontend Review Application Gateway ingress, certificate ownership, WAF policy and cost before opting in

Set mapped scalar inputs with azd env set. Native arrays/objects such as the complete address plan, allowedIpRanges, Storage controls and publicIngress belong in the reviewed root main.parameters.json, not invented environment variables. In the Agent platform, hooks regenerate infra/main.parameters.json; do not edit that generated copy. The parameter reference describes foundation inputs; Agent configuration describes platform composition and overrides.

docs.title: Bind the future application (Agent source only)
docs.text:
Choose the orchestrator topology and ingestion selection now, even if images will be deployed later. For a different application:

azd env set AGENTLZ_APP_DEFINITION <path-to-app-definition.json>

Otherwise use the bundled definition. The first provision binds the environment to its application ID; a different ID requires a new environment. Keep the existing topology and ingestion selection on upgrades.

docs.title: Step 4: Preview and provision
docs.text:
For Agent source, first run azd hooks run preup to validate the definition and binding before azd's resource-group initialization. Then, in either source:

azd provision --preview
azd provision

Review the preview's scopes, names, routes, resource changes, public access and role assignments before the second command. Resolve quota, Policy, subnet and capacity findings rather than skipping preflight. Preview is not an application or connectivity test.

Source What provisioning completes Agent platform Validation and binding, foundation deployment, then service configuration, role reconciliation and App Configuration publication unless explicitly deferred Upstream Bicep foundation Foundation preflight and resource deployment; no Agent post-provision modules or application image deployment

Selected Container Apps can run placeholder images at this point. An upstream hello-world response proves only that network/runtime smoke test. It is not evidence of Agent authentication, tools, ingestion or document authorization.

docs.title: Verify the foundation
docs.text:
Inspect the intended environment and selected resources:

azd env get-value AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID
azd env get-value AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP
az resource list -g <resource-group> --query "[].{name:name,type:type}" -o table
az network private-endpoint list -g <resource-group> \
  --query "[].{name:name,state:provisioningState,connections:privateLinkServiceConnections[].privateLinkServiceConnectionState.status}" -o json

Compare the inventory with enabled features and reuse inputs, not a fixed resource count. For private deployments, verify approved connections, private DNS resolution and TCP/TLS reachability from the actual deployment host. Then test each required data plane with its authorized identity and confirm telemetry reaches the intended workspace. See the standalone checks and hub-specific checks.

docs.title: Platform outputs (Agent source only)
docs.text:
After configuration completes, App Configuration publishes the JSON AGENTLZ_PLATFORM_OUTPUTS and matching flat keys under label agent-lz. Search and Cosmos sections are omitted when their endpoints are absent; other required fields must validate. These derived keys are not written back to the azd environment.

Flat key JSON path AGENTLZ_FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT foundry.projectEndpoint AGENTLZ_FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT_NAME foundry.accountName AGENTLZ_ACR_LOGIN_SERVER registry.loginServer AGENTLZ_APPCONFIG_ENDPOINT appConfig.endpoint AGENTLZ_SEARCH_ENDPOINT search.endpoint AGENTLZ_STORAGE_BLOB_ENDPOINT storage.blobEndpoint AGENTLZ_COSMOS_ENDPOINT cosmos.endpoint AGENTLZ_KEYVAULT_URI keyVault.uri

AGENTLZ_NETWORK_ISOLATED records isolation. AGENTLZ_IDENTITY_<COMPONENT>_CLIENT_ID and the JSON identities array contain discovered Container App identity client IDs, not principal IDs. Hosted runtime identities are created later, during application deployment. Missing or ambiguous identities fail publication; system-assigned identity resolution also requires the exact Entra service-principal read. AGENTLZ_COMPONENT_IDENTITIES is an explicit override input, not an automatic output.

az appconfig kv show --endpoint <app-configuration-endpoint> \
  --key AGENTLZ_PLATFORM_OUTPUTS --label agent-lz --auth-mode login

If only output publication needs refreshing after successful configuration:

azd env refresh
python -m config.deployment.outputs

This does not replace deferred or failed service configuration.

docs.title: Complete a deferred post-provision
docs.text:
For Agent source, private configuration can be explicitly deferred by RUN_FROM_JUMPBOX=false, or by AZURE_SKIP_NETWORK_ISOLATION_WARNING=true when RUN_FROM_JUMPBOX is not truthy. Set the approved deferral before the first provision when the connected host does not exist yet. Successful provisioning then reports that application setup is incomplete. Deferral does not bypass earlier topology/private-service checks.

On a new connected host, restore the same reviewed source revision and root parameter file. Install the prerequisites and Python dependencies, authenticate both CLIs, then initialize local state only if absent:

azd env new <same-environment-name>
azd env set AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID <subscription-id>
azd env set AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP <existing-resource-group>
azd env set AZURE_LOCATION <region>
azd env refresh

If the environment is already present, select it instead. Reapply the approved deployment inputs: refresh restores outputs, not your full configuration. Do not publish or copy another stage's .azure/ state as an input artifact. Managed-identity sign-in is an option for an appropriately authorized runner, not proof that its configuration/build roles are sufficient.

From the connected host, clear deferral and finish configuration:

azd env set RUN_FROM_JUMPBOX true
azd env set AZURE_SKIP_NETWORK_ISOLATION_WARNING false
azd hooks run postprovision

RUN_FROM_JUMPBOX requests checks; it does not provide connectivity. Verify platform outputs and required data-plane access before deploying. Private native Blob sources can require an administrator to approve the exact Search shared private-link request reported by the readiness gate. Do not approve every pending connection or bypass the gate.

docs.title: Reconfigure or upgrade the foundation
docs.text:
Record the deployed source revision, approved parameters, outputs and dependent applications. Back up required data and configuration, review the new source's migrations and retain existing names, locations, topology and ingestion intent. Review preview before applying approved root parameter changes with the provisioning step above.

For Agent environments, integrate the coordinated platform and its infra/ tree together; do not replace only its foundation folder with upstream main. See platform upgrades and rollback. Upstream foundation environments use their own source and complete root parameter contract, without Agent post-provision commands.

Retry a partial deployment with the same approved revision and environment after repairing the specific failure. Reverting code is not guaranteed to reverse resource or data changes. Do not delete data, rename subnets, move existing resources to another region, weaken isolation or bypass preflight to recover. Turning a deploy flag off is not deletion or permission cleanup.

docs.title: Add an application later
docs.text: In an Agent foundation, deploy the same bound application and selected components. Follow Step 4 of the full-stack runbook: classic can deploy after configuration; bundled hosted needs image preparation and a second provision first. Custom definitions follow their own component contract. An upstream-only foundation is not a configured Agent environment.

docs.title: Remove the foundation
docs.text: Use the safe environment removal procedure from this source's root and selected environment. Confirm ownership and backups before deletion. For a spoke, have network/DNS owners remove only the recorded spoke-specific attachments and preserve shared services. Purge is a separate irreversible decision, not a normal retry or rollback.

docs.title: Hosted agents
docs.text:
The orchestrator runs your selected agent strategy as a Foundry hosted agent or a Container App. Hosting controls where it runs. Strategies control how it coordinates models, retrieval and tools. Changing one does not automatically change the other.

Use this page to choose a topology and understand its contracts. Execute the ordered procedure in Deploy the full stack, or stop at the foundation with Deploy infrastructure only.

docs.title: Topologies
docs.text:
DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY Orchestrator runs as Administrative panel Application Cosmos DB hosted-no-panel (fresh default) Foundry hosted agent Not deployed Not deployed hosted-panel Foundry hosted agent Deployed Deployed classic Container App Not applicable Deployed

This table describes the bundled application, not resources retained after a migration. In hosted-panel, application Cosmos DB stores owner-index and feedback metadata, not hosted transcripts. Foundry Agent Service can have its own backing Cosmos DB. Continuity and history need separate configuration.

Topology resolution

  • An explicit DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY selects the topology.
  • New environments default to hosted-no-panel.
  • Existing environments retain a recorded topology.
  • Older environments without a topology marker resolve to classic, rather than silently moving an existing runtime.

Choose before provisioning, for example:

azd env set DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY hosted-panel

Ingestion selection is independent of all three topologies. Native source ingestion does not replace conversation uploads or the application's SharePoint jobs. See Ingestion and conversation uploads.

docs.title: Image and deployment handoff
docs.text:
A hosted deployment separates foundation provisioning, image preparation and agent-version deployment. Preparation builds the manifest-pinned orchestrator, resolves it to an immutable digest and adds the supported hosted startup command. Provisioning then records that digest in the deployment handoff. Provisioning alone does not create a running agent version.

Follow the full-stack runbook for the exact initial sequence. A fresh azd up does not build a missing hosted image or replace the required handoff provision. Private builds use the VNet's ACR Tasks agent pool.

docs.title: Redeploy the same image or prepare a new one
docs.text:
Change Required behavior Same digest, compatible source and provisioned handoff Deployment can reuse the image. Changed manifest orchestrator commit Prepare a new generated image and provision its handoff before deployment. Deploy-only does not rebuild it or check generated source provenance against the new manifest. Changed process environment in hosted-agent/azure.yaml Deploy a new agent version, potentially using the same digest. Running versions are not mutated. Explicit digest without generated-source provenance You manage compatibility and registry availability. Preparation does not automatically replace it when source pins change.

Generated images are reused only when recorded source and startup-command provenance match. Preparation with --image-version sha256:<64-hex-characters> skips building and clears generated provenance. Promoting identical source pins does not prove that independently built images have identical digests.

Use application redeployment or the upgrade workflow.

docs.title: Validation rules
docs.text:
Setting Contract HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE_VERSION Immutable sha256: digest followed by 64 hexadecimal characters. Image tags are rejected. HOSTED_AGENT_RESOURCE_SCOPE Explicit delegated-user audience ending in /.default, supplied before provisioning. It is not the UI's own API scope. HOSTED_AGENT_STARTUP_COMMAND Fixed to uvicorn src.api.hosted_entrypoint:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8088. Custom values are rejected. HOSTED_AGENT_SSE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS Stream idle timeout, default 60. HOSTED_CONTINUITY_ENABLED Default false. Requests separately validated continuity activation, not generic runtime history. PRESERVE_CLASSIC_RUNTIME Default false. Can retain classic orchestration during a reviewed hosted migration.

The bundled child hosted-agent/azure.yaml declares agent name, CPU, memory, protocols and startup command as literal fields. Similarly named provisioning inputs do not automatically customize those fields. Deliberate child-definition changes must remain compatible with the provisioning contract.

For a custom definition, source.imageDigest becomes AGENTLZ_IMAGE_DIGEST. It is not interchangeable with the bundled HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE_VERSION. See Custom applications.

docs.title: Bootstrap the agent's runtime access
docs.text:
These identities serve different purposes:

Identity Responsibility Deployment principal Provisions resources, authors agent versions and reconciles authorized scoped grants. Foundry project managed identity Pulls the image using the foundation's registry grant. Actual deployed agent runtime principal Reads its runtime configuration and calls authorized services. Delegated user Needs caller/agent access and permission to the requested data.

The bundled post-deploy hook discovers the actual runtime principal and grants App Configuration Data Reader on the store and Cognitive Services OpenAI User on the Foundry account. If AUDIT_HMAC_KEY is a Key Vault reference, it also plans Key Vault Secrets User on that individual secret. This is a closed bootstrap set, not every component capability profile or a caller-access grant.

The deployment principal needs scoped role-assignment authority. Alternatively, an authorized administrator can review and apply the exact read-only plan. Do not grant resource-group/subscription Owner or remove unrelated assignments to resolve a denial. ARM grant visibility is not proof of data-plane readiness. Allow propagation and use hosted access recovery.

Custom hosted services instead reconcile their declared capability profiles against their discovered runtime principal. See Capability profiles.

docs.title: Configure the UI's delegated authentication
docs.text:
The UI defaults to HOSTED_AGENT_AUTH_MODE=user_delegated. It exchanges the signed-in user's token using OAuth on-behalf-of (OBO), with no fallback to the UI managed identity. Publish these settings under App Configuration label agent-lz before accepting user sign-in:

Key Value OAUTH_AZURE_AD_CLIENT_ID Confidential Entra application's client ID. OAUTH_AZURE_AD_TENANT_ID Its tenant ID. OAUTH_AZURE_AD_CLIENT_SECRET Key Vault reference, never plaintext. OAUTH_AZURE_AD_SCOPES api://<client-id>/user_impersonation openid profile offline_access for the UI's single-token login. CHAINLIT_URL Canonical HTTPS frontend origin without a trailing slash.

Expose user_impersonation, request version-2 access tokens and register the exact HTTPS /auth/oauth/azure-ad/callback redirect URI. Separately configure and consent the downstream delegated permissions for the deployed Foundry audience. A Graph token or the UI's API scope is not Foundry OBO consent.

Verify the user path

A successful managed-identity greeting does not prove login, OBO or document authorization. Test real-user invocation and document allow/deny behavior, and verify unauthenticated panel requests are rejected. The panel has no development authentication bypass.

Callbacks, credentials and panel requirements

Behind TLS-terminating ingress, explicitly set CHAINLIT_URL. Check that /auth/oauth/azure-ad redirects with the exact registered HTTPS callback. Fix an HTTP callback by correcting the canonical URL and restarting the UI, not by registering an insecure redirect.

With hosted-panel and ingestion selected, ingestion also needs the OAuth tenant and client ID. Follow tenant credential-lifetime policy, record expiration and rotate the Key Vault credential before it expires. A stable, protected CHAINLIT_AUTH_SECRET prevents session resets from a newly generated temporary signing secret.

docs.title: Protocol and caller access
docs.text:
• Responses 2.0.0 is stateless. A non-null previous_response_id returns HTTP 422. Top-level conversation and other unhandled routing/sampling fields do not load history. Supply bounded, ordered input ending in the user message.
  • The bundled UI uses /invocations?api-version=v1. Its conversation_id labels conversation-scoped retrieval, not permission to load managed history. The UI accepts response.conversation.id and the compatibility response.conversation_id; malformed or conflicting IDs fail explicitly.
  • A delegated caller needs Foundry user access on the project and agent access. Deployment permission alone does not provide this.

For Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot, follow Publish to Teams and M365. It uses Bot Service authorization and the Foundry Activity endpoint, not the UI's delegated invocation path.

For a Copilot Studio agent calling a private Foundry hosted agent, follow Connect Copilot Studio. It uses a Power Automate agent flow with an authenticated HTTPS connection and VNet delegation, not the native connected-agent tool. Review its shared-connection identity boundary before using it with protected data.

Continuity, history and the administrative panel

Without continuity, hosted multi-turn context in the active UI session is not durable history after reload, browser restart or a new chat. Hosted mode does not register the classic orchestrator/Dapr history data layer. Login, chat and feedback callbacks remain available.

When enabled and activated, continuity coordinates managed Conversations reads/writes in the UI with owner binding and agent-scoped permissions. It sends the authorized transcript to the stateless runtime; it does not grant the container general history access.

Panel history needs DEPLOY_ADMINISTRATIVE_PANEL, PANEL_HISTORY_ENABLED and hosted continuity, plus authentication and owner checks. Disabled history surfaces return HTTP 503. Cosmos owner-index/feedback data is metadata, not a second transcript store. A topology or enabled flag alone proves neither persistence nor cross-user isolation.

docs.title: Configuration TLS compatibility
docs.text:
APP_CONFIG_TLS_COMPATIBILITY is an opt-in process environment variable, default false, read before remote configuration can load. Consider it only after verifying private connectivity when App Configuration or Key Vault TLS handshakes stall. It applies to the orchestrator loader, not every HTTP client.

When enabled, the profile uses P-256 and TCP MSS 1200 only for the configured App Configuration and application Key Vault endpoints. Certificate/hostname verification, custom CAs, TLS 1.2 or later, credentials and retries remain intact. It requires the actual HTTPS KEY_VAULT_URI; missing URI or invalid boolean fails startup.

Change the process input and deploy a new agent version using the redeployment runbook. An App Configuration key cannot replace this bootstrap input. Disable the profile to revert it and redeploy. Never disable certificate validation or infer a proven MTU root cause from a successful compatibility test. See TLS diagnosis.

docs.title: Telemetry and topology changes
docs.text:
Prompt/completion capture in telemetry is off by default. Enable it only when your organization's policy permits storing that content in Application Insights.

During a migration preserving classic runtime, routing stays classic until HOSTED_AGENT_BASE_URL, a valid digest and HOSTED_CUTOVER_COMPLETE=true are present. Cutover markers record hook completion, not user acceptance. A failed greeting or selected component deployment blocks cutover.

To change topology, use the full-stack runbook, then verify routing, intended revisions, authentication, source bindings and authorization. Selecting classic does not select ingestion or delete a hosted agent. The legacy DEPLOY_HOSTED_AGENT_ORCHESTRATION=false selects classic only when DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY is absent and the legacy flag pair is consistent. Retiring the old runtime is a separate decision.

docs.title: How the template works
docs.text: Agent Landing Zone connects deployment inputs, Azure infrastructure and agent application code through the Azure Developer CLI (azd). This page explains that connection for the Bicep/azd implementation. Use the deployment runbooks for the commands to execute.

docs.title: Repository boundaries
docs.text:
The platform repository composes the solution. It does not contain every application's runtime source.

Area Responsibility Foundation: platform infra/ Repository-owned Bicep source for Azure resources, identities and access. manifest.json → infra.source records the upstream AI Landing Zone source it incorporates. Platform integration: root files, scripts/ and config/ Selects the application, composes deployment parameters, configures provisioned services and coordinates deployment. Runtime component repositories Own the UI, agent strategies and tools, and optional application ingestion code. The manifest identifies their repositories and source pins.

The infra.source entry is provenance, not a separately deployed package or submodule. Deploy the platform's reviewed infra/ tree, including its platform changes, rather than substituting an upstream infrastructure tag.

docs.title: The manifest records a validated combination
docs.text:
manifest.json records the platform release and each bundled component's repository, ref and exact commit. It is the authoritative source for the coordinated combination; the documentation does not maintain a second component-version table.

The hooks fetch selected bundled Container App components into sibling directories and verify their commits. Hosted image preparation fetches the pinned orchestrator separately for its build. You do not need to fork every repository to deploy the unmodified application.

If you change component source, its repository and the platform's pins must agree. The bundled app-definition.json also declares component source pins and is validated against the manifest. A modified combination needs its own integration validation. See Custom applications for repository customization and pinning rules.

docs.title: Parameters describe the environment
docs.text:
The checked-in root main.parameters.json maps deployment inputs to infrastructure parameters. Values can be literals or references to the selected azd environment's variables. Inline defaults apply where declared; other unset inputs can use Bicep defaults.

Before provisioning, the hooks resolve the selected application and hosting topology, apply the environment inputs and generate infra/main.parameters.json. Bicep consumes that generated file.

Edit the source, not the generated output

Use documented deployment inputs and the root parameter file. Do not edit infra/main.parameters.json; the next composition can overwrite it. See Configuration for the available inputs and defaults.

An application definition describes the selected application's components and capabilities. Select a custom definition before the first provision: one azd environment is bound to one application ID. It is not a late switch that changes only the deployment command.

Hosting, orchestration strategy and ingestion selection are separate decisions. For example, choosing a hosted orchestrator does not select an ingestion path. The configuration and application definition must form a supported combination.

docs.title: azure.yaml connects azd to the lifecycle
docs.text:
The root azure.yaml points azd at infra/ and registers PowerShell and shell lifecycle hooks. Those hooks run the platform's configuration modules and coordinate the child application projects.

Stage What the platform does Before azd up (preup) Validates the application definition and checks its environment binding. Before provisioning (preprovision) Resolves application selection and topology, composes infrastructure parameters and runs preflight checks. After provisioning (postprovision) Configures Azure services, reconciles application access and publishes runtime settings and outputs. Before deployment (predeploy) Checks foundation readiness and application binding, validates topology and required connectivity, then coordinates the selected application deployments.

azd provision therefore includes service configuration through its post-provision hook. It does not mean the pinned application code is running: some provisioned Container Apps initially contain placeholder images.

For bundled Container Apps, deployment uses the verified component checkouts and their child azure.yaml projects to build and deploy the code. Hosted orchestration uses the prepared image described below. Custom applications provide their own definition and child project.

docs.title: App Configuration carries runtime settings
docs.text:
Deployment inputs describe what to create. Runtime settings describe how applications use the resulting services.

Provisioning and configuration publish settings to Azure App Configuration under the agent-lz label. Runtime components read that label, while bootstrap values such as the store endpoint must be available before remote configuration can load. Secrets belong in Key Vault and are referenced rather than copied into checked-in settings.

The label is a shared convention, not an environment boundary. Keep development, test and production configuration, identities and data separated, following the environment boundaries guidance. Local .azure/ state is private deployment state, not a source-controlled input file; the hooks also copy state into child projects, so protect those workspaces.

See Configuration for setting names, sources and restart requirements.

docs.title: Why hosted agents need image preparation
docs.text:
A Foundry hosted agent needs an immutable image before its agent version can be deployed. That creates a bootstrap dependency on the registry and Foundry resources.

  1. Create the prerequisites. Initial provisioning establishes the foundation and runs its service configuration.
  2. Prepare the image. The preparation script builds the pinned orchestrator and a derived image with the supported hosted entrypoint, then records the image digest and build provenance.
  3. Record the handoff. A further provision materializes the immutable deployment handoff using that digest.
  4. Deploy the application. Deployment creates the hosted agent version and deploys the other selected application components.

Image preparation does not start the agent, and provisioning does not create the running data-plane agent version. Deploy-only reuses a compatible prepared image rather than rebuilding changed orchestrator source.

The same source pins do not guarantee the same image digest when images are built independently. If a promotion process requires the identical image, preserve and verify its digest and registry availability separately.

For execution steps, use Deploy the full stack. For strategy eligibility and image behavior, see Agent hosting.

docs.title: From understanding to deployment
docs.text: Review the design checklist, then choose Deploy infrastructure only or Deploy the full stack. Those runbooks contain the prerequisites, topology-specific sequence and validation steps.

docs.title: Ingestion and conversation uploads
docs.text:
Source ingestion prepares documents for retrieval. Conversation uploads attach files to an individual chat. They have different configuration and authorization requirements.

Choosing where the orchestrator runs does not choose either path. An agent strategy controls orchestration behavior, not whether an ingestion service is deployed.

docs.title: Choose a source ingestion path
docs.text:
Path What processes the source When to use it Native Foundry IQ Blob source Azure AI Search processes the configured azureBlob knowledge source Your documents and permission model fit the supported native Blob configuration. No ingestion Container App is required for this path.
